work=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf -- "$work"' EXIT; printf 'const x: number = 42; console.log(x);\n' > "$work/main.ts"; "$OFFLINE_PREFIX/bin/bun" build --target bun --outfile "$work/app.js" "$work/main.ts"; test "$("$OFFLINE_PREFIX/bin/bun" "$work/app.js")" = 42
notes: Converted the original https://bun.sh/install script, snapshot SHA256 04882bf41679d49d9af108657a1e5515bf04fdf2940d12c0d0b1e5d79dc53be8. Current latest tag resolved to bun-v1.4.4 on 2026-11-09.
Pinned Ubuntu 22.04 x86_64 glibc and linux-x64-baseline; download replaced with exact local resource lookup. Original extraction, shell setup and completion behavior retained.
Four unquoted completion executable invocations were quoted to handle installation directories containing spaces. Completion and bunx generation are actually executed in smoke checks.
Bundled Ubuntu unzip and libbz2 debs are extracted to a temporary private directory by dpkg-deb, not installed system-wide. No sudo, Python, curl, wget or preinstalled unzip is needed on the target.
Generated install.sh defaults to OFFLINE_PREFIX, then BUN_INSTALL, then HOME/.bun. --prefix overrides the default. Existing Bash/Zsh/Fish profile handling follows the official script.
Scope is Bun runtime and installation-time resources, including local shell completions. Arbitrary project packages, bun install dependencies and bunx package downloads are not included.
